row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that self-predictions miss individual cells by about 8 rating points or more (noise or per-cell bias), which equals the no-uptake guess's error because most measured shifts are small.
row.failure_reason: Self-predictions beat no uptake on the own-answer cells (5.1 vs 8.9 points), but on the other-person cells they sat 17.2 points from Haiku's usual rating on average against 8.8 for its real re-ratings, so their error (13.3) cancelled the own-cell advantage; pooled +0.33 [-3.08, +4.07]. Kind world.
row.result: On Haiku's 324 archived uptake cells, its self-predictions missed its real re-ratings by 9.17 rating points against 8.85 for a no-effect guess (+0.33, BCa [-3.08, +4.07], jackknife-t [-3.76, +4.41]): fail; better on own-answer cells, worse on other-person cells.
row.diagnosis: On this archive Haiku's self-predictions do not beat a no-effect guess cell by cell; they track the own-answer pull well and over-scatter on another person's number. Open (audit, about $0.055): a base-prediction arm to separate misjudging its usual rating from misjudging its quirk.
row.models_note: archive only: no model is in the loop (rule 12)
row.scoring_note: Scored on the pre-registered rule as fixed before data (D17b, D17c): engine odds 0.10 (map 0.55; 0.18 at prereg; 0.10 re-stated before data), human odds 0.70 (card framed at effect level; card_event_effect_level_pass true). Audit 59ff14e stands, 5 cuts applied D17e; pl-033 clean. $0.
row.human_odds_event_note: Sean's 0.70 (ho-20261105-061152-bxe) was given on a card whose framing came from om-p2-4's effect-level numbers; the effect-level reading of the event would almost certainly pass on om-p2-4's published table (self 0.064 against 0.297). row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that Sam's excess over the model's own re-rating comes only from upward plants on both models, as on Haiku, so the downward-plant gap's interval reaches 0.
row.failure_reason: Neither model showed any Sam-over-own excess, upward or downward (Sonnet upward +0.001 [-0.042, +0.049], Opus +0.089 [-0.044, +0.259]; both read none); Sam's rating moved toward the planted number about as much as the model's own re-rating and about as much as toward Alex's number. Kind world.
row.result: On Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (2 repeats, om-p2-5's 16 vignettes), Sam's rating did not move further than the model's own re-rating in either direction (readings none, none): fail; Haiku's 'Sam moves more than self' did not replicate.
row.diagnosis: Haiku's Sam-over-self excess does not replicate on Sonnet or Opus on this design. Open (audit, about $1.10): the anchors rival (Haiku's anchors on the other models), Sonnet with its own anchors.

row.odds_reason: other-minds 0/9 and layer 1 1/14 outweigh engine-source 0.58; same engine, same days, 11/17 patterns program-1, so siblings likely share traps; 15-point gap needs large effect.
row.odds_event: Program 2's share of its 22 misses and required audit cuts carrying a pattern recorded first in program 1 (origins file, 11 of 17) is >= 0.50 and >= 0.15 above the share among programs 4-6's 74 units, as tagged by fresh classifier A
row.seed_note: no draw; packet order by a fixed constant 20261105

design_review.note: fixes applied (D21a); the F4 pilot then parked the bet (D21b) before confirmation was needed

row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that the program-1 patterns are generic design faults (power, baselines, bundled comparisons, wording) that programs 4–6 commit as often as program 2, so the difference stays under 15 points.
row.diagnosis: Untestable as built: by the fresh origin coding 11 of the engine's 17 recorded traps were already in program 1's pre-gate work, so a gap in program 2's failures cannot be tied to program 1's traps rather than to the unit mix. Needs an origin-specific pattern list, or two seed questions run in parallel from scratch (proposal Q4).
row.models_note: no model is tested; the object is the engine's record (rule 12)
row.scoring_note: parked before any test unit was tagged, by D21a's pre-registered rule: the dry run on the pilot's measured tag sets passes at most 0.003 (the origin-permutation condition has no power when 11 of 17 patterns are program 1's)

row.lesson: Correcting P3 and P15: om-p2-4's gate was passed by a know-nothing predictor. This bet scores self-prediction against the no-uptake guess in rating points, chosen after a dry run on program 1's measured cells showed uptake units let tiny displacements decide, and its odds are 18% (from 55% on the map) because zero is strong where shifts are small.
row.design_change: primary error in rating points, not uptake units, after a dry run on program 1's measured cells (synthetic predictions, P2-4 cache unopened) showed uptake units let |D| near 0.05 cells decide (P15); the no-uptake and copy dumb predictors scored on the same cells (P3); dry run P(pass) 1.00 / 0.79 / 0.00 at 5 / 7.5 / 10 points of noise (P12); 1e-9 boundary (P13); leave-one-vignette-out re-applies the rule (P10); vignette is the resampling unit (P14)
row.odds_reason: other-minds 0/7 and literature 2/15 rows; dry run passes only below ~7.5 points of prediction noise against an 8.85-point no-uptake error, with a 16-item bootstrap.
row.odds_note: Two fresh rule-14 contexts: the first was given the design with uptake units as primary and said 0.32 - 0.12 = 0.20; after the dry run moved the primary to rating points, a second, given the final design, said 0.32 - 0.14 = 0.18, which is the bet's odds. The author had read Sean's 0.70 before the odds; neither fresh context saw it.
row.scored_note: Audit 59ff14e. P3 partly held: the no-uptake and copy dumb predictors were scored, but the bet adopted no margin over the dumb guess ('beat it by a margin' not adopted; E25 note). P15 recurred until D17c: the dry-run worlds were assumptions until the design review's calibrated worlds were cited, and every world built the self-prediction on the measured base, so the fail cannot separate misjudging the usual rating from misjudging the shift (design_review_missed D4/D7). P12 held (the bet could go either way; it failed). P13 held. P10 held (0 flips). The odds moved 0.55 -> 0.18 -> 0.10 before a miss.

row.lesson: Correcting P10 and P1: om-p2-5's pooled gap hid that only upward plants carried it, and a novelty story is not odds. This bet scores each plant direction as its own conjunct on Sonnet and Opus, with a dry run passing 0.85 at a clear two-way gap and 0.23 Haiku-like, and its odds are 12% (none on the map) because the downward gap was null.
row.design_change: the up/down split is the primary (each direction its own conjunct), not a post hoc audit split (P10); dry run over named worlds: pass 0.85 clear two-way gap, 0.23 Haiku-like, ~0 Sam = own (P12); per-model readings, no cross-model comparison sentence (P8); 1e-9 bounds (P13); vignette bootstrap (P14)
row.odds_reason: other-minds 0/7, literature 0.13 and model referee 0.22 outweigh layer-2/$1-5 rows; parent's downward gap was null, Opus uptake ~0.07, and Haiku-like dry run passes only 0.23.
row.odds_note: No map odds were stated for P2-5r (the direction was added with its card at 9099bdd). Lesson sentence is 64 words, over the 60-word limit (D18a).
row.scored_note: Audit 5b66ecb. P10 held in the split (each direction its own conjunct) but recurred in a new form: one statement (Sonnet co-lin06 X, reference 30 against Haiku's anchor 85) decided Sonnet's reading through extreme uptake ratios (design_review_missed D5: uptake divides by distance from Haiku's anchor but measures from the model's own reference). P8 recurred in the write-up (a cross-model comparison, cut 4). P1 held: odds 0.12/0.15 before a miss. P12, P13, P14 held.

row.lesson: Correcting P8 and P3: program 2 was seeded by program 1, so this is not a test of independent seeds, and a share any tagging could reach says nothing. This bet fixes each pattern's origin before any tag and reports the any-pattern share and a second classifier, and its odds are 30% (from 50% on the map) because wording cuts count as not program 1.
row.design_change: pattern origins fixed by a written rule before any tag and never shown to the classifier (P8: the seeds are coupled, stated); the any-pattern share, pattern counts and a second classifier reported beside the program-1 share (P3); leave-one-bet-out (P10); frozen sentence (P9); 1e-9 bar (P13)
row.odds_reason: other-minds 0/8 and layer 1 1/14 pull down, engine source 0.58 pulls up; 16 of 22 units are audit cuts, and the commonest cut class, wording, counts as not program 1.
row.odds_note: Lesson sentence is 65 words, over the 60-word limit; frozen as written.

row.lesson: Correcting P2 and P12: om-p2-4's null rule had no margin and could not see the gap it called absent. This bet fixes a ±0.05 equivalence margin with a power check on the parent's archive (exchangeable labels pass 0.98), and its odds are 10% (from 20% on the map) because that archive reads self-better in every resample.
row.design_change: ±0.05 equivalence margin on the BCa interval with a power dry run on om-p2-4's archived predictions (exchangeable labels pass 0.98; as archived self-better 1.00) (P2, P12); worlds from the archive, not assumptions (P15); vignette bootstrap and leave-one-out (P14, P10); 1e-9 bounds (P13); Sonnet/Opus truth measured here (P8)
row.odds_reason: Dry run on archived parent reads self-better 100% (pass 0%); tight ±0.05 equivalence over 16 vignettes; other-minds 0/8, literature 0.12, model referee 0.21 outweigh layer-2/$1-5 rows.

row.lesson: Correcting P3 and P8: om-p2-path's share had no baseline and its origin coding decided the result. This bet compares program 2 with three siblings program 1 did not seed, by origins a fresh session fixed, and its odds are 15% (from 50% on the map) because siblings share most traps and the gap must be 15 points.
row.design_change: baseline of programs 4-6 tagged in the same shuffled packet and a 15-point margin (P3); origins fixed by a fresh session under one dated gate, unedited (the withdrawn bet's P9 decision); coupling stated (P8); leave-one-bet-out (P10); dry run on real counts (P12); 1e-9 bar (P13)
row.odds_reason: other-minds 0/9 and layer 1 1/14 outweigh engine-source 0.58; same engine, same days, 11/17 patterns program-1, so siblings likely share traps; 15-point gap needs large effect.
